content: 1. The active metabolite of sofosbuvir, GS-331007, is responsible for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. 2. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely if co-administration is necessary. 3. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of rosuvastatin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Co-administration may increase the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 4. Safinamide increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by inhibiting intestinal breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP). Use caution and monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects of BCRP substrates. 5. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates, which may require dosage reduction. 6. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels of seladelpar through an unspecified mechanism. Monitor for adverse effects if co-administered with BCRP inhibitors. 7. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. 8. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage modifications. 9. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. P-gp inducers reduce sofosbuvir levels and its conversion to the active metabolite GS-331007. 10. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and as a BCRP transport inhibitor. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Consider dosage reduction for BCRP substrates if adverse effects occur. 11. Tafamidis increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by inhibiting BCRP in vitro, potentially increasing exposure to BCRP substrates. Dosage adjustment of these substrates may be necessary. 12. Talazoparib levels may increase when co-administered with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir due to inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely, as talazoparib is a P-gp substrate, and systemic exposure may increase. 13. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its product labeling. 15. Tipranavir decreases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. P-gp inducers reduce sofosbuvir levels and its conversion to the active metabolite GS-331007. 16. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of topotecan via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Oral topotecan product labeling recommends avoiding P-gp inhibitors; the interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 17. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. 18. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing exposure to BCRP substrates. Monitor for signs of adverse effects and reduce substrate doses as per product labeling. 19. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of venetoclax via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a P-gp inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for toxicities. 20. Patients should be tested for current or prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection before initiating treatment with hepatitis C direct-acting antivirals (DAAs). HBV reactivation has been reported in HCV/HBV co-infected patients undergoing or completing DAA treatment without HBV antiviral therapy, with some cases resulting in fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, or death. Monitor for hepatitis flare or HBV reactivation during and after HCV treatment, and initiate appropriate management for HBV infection as clinically indicated. 21. If co-administered with ribavirin, the contraindications to ribavirin also apply to this combination regimen. The combination is contraindicated in pregnant women and in men whose female partners are pregnant. Reliable contraception must be used during and after treatment (9 months for women, 6 months for men). 22. There is no adequate human data to establish whether the drug combination poses a risk to pregnancy outcomes. Animal studies have shown no evidence of adverse developmental outcomes at exposures greater than those in humans at the recommended dose. 23. It is unknown whether ledipasvir, sofosbuvir, or their metabolites are present in human breast milk, affect milk production, or have effects on the breastfed infant. The benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and potential adverse effects on the infant. 24. Ledipasvir inhibits the HCV NS5A protein, essential for viral replication, while sofosbuvir, a nucleotide prodrug, is metabolized to an active uridine analog triphosphate that inhibits the HCV NS5B RNA-dependent polymerase, suppressing viral replication. 25. Sofosbuvir undergoes extensive hepatic metabolism to form the active nucleoside analog triphosphate GS-461203, with dephosphorylation resulting in GS-331007, which accounts for <90% of total systemic exposure. 26. Antacids and acid-lowering medications (e.g., famotidine, omeprazole) reduce ledipasvir absorption and may impair its efficacy. 27. Common side effects include tiredness, headache, nausea, diarrhea, and difficulty sleeping. Serious allergic reactions are rare. 28. Store tablets and oral pellets at room temperature (<30°C) in their original container. Do not store in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication. 29. If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is less than 6 hours before the next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. 30. Overdose management includes contacting emergency services or a poison control center immediately. 31. Laboratory tests (e.g., liver function, hepatitis B and C tests) should be performed before, during, and after treatment.
